integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: fire on P-7111 during cleaning and preparation

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an organisational factor.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the secondary containment by bund and drainage on P-7111 and PT-7111 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in responding to a loss of containment, specifically isolating and depressuring a leaking system. P-7111 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during cleaning and preparation while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 22 March 2007 an incident occurred on P-7111 and PT-7111 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during cleaning and preparation, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
